hook.text: Planet Fitness charges $10/month. At 18 million members, that model works when most never show up.

buildup.text: Gym franchises profit from sign-ups, not visits. The business model is selling access, not exercise.

discovery.text: Planet Fitness offers free pizza Mondays. They actively discourage intense athletes who intimidate casuals.

twist.text: CrossFit charges $200/month for tiny gyms. Opposite model: high price, intense culture, loyal community.

climax.text: Gym franchises span from Planet Fitness to CrossFit. The market supports opposite strategies simultaneously.

punchline.text: $10/month, free pizza, 18 million members. Most don't use the gym.

quiz.question: Why does Planet Fitness offer free pizza?
options: To discourage intense athletes and keep a casual atmosphere

details.summary: Gym franchises like Planet Fitness, Anytime Fitness, and Orangetheory scale rapidly by offering different price points and workout experiences..
details.whyItMatters: The gym franchise model is built on behavioral economics. It only works because most members overestimate their future attendance. Understanding this reveals how subscription businesses can profit from the gap between intention and behavior.
takeaways: Gym profitability depends on members who pay but rarely attend the facility
Planet Fitness pioneered the low-cost high-volume no-intimidation model
Boutique fitness franchises charge premium prices for specialized group experiences

faq.question: Why do gym franchises need non-attending members to be profitable?
faq.answer: Physical capacity limits the number of people who can use a gym simultaneously. If all members showed up regularly, the gym would be overcrowded. Low-attendance members subsidize facility costs and keep prices affordable. Gyms typically sell 5 to 10 times more memberships than peak capacity.

faq.question: What are the different gym franchise models?
faq.answer: Budget gyms like Planet Fitness charge 10 to 25 dollars monthly for basic equipment access. Mid-range gyms like Anytime Fitness offer 24-hour access and personal training. Boutique franchises like Orangetheory and F45 charge 100-plus monthly for specialized group classes.
